body.claim: The second hand of an analog clock can appear to stay still for longer than normal when you first look at it.
body.why: After a quick eye movement (a saccade), the new target can seem to have been seen for longer, and this can extend apparent durations by up to half a second. During a saccade, visual information is suppressed, and the gap in perception is “filled in” with information gathered after the saccade.

probes.question: By up to how much can this effect extend apparent durations?
True or false: visual information collected during a saccade is suppressed.

image_brief.show: An analog wall clock with a visible second hand

claims.claim: Title/claim: second hand of an analog clock can appear to stay still for longer than normal when first looked at (stopped-clock illusion)
claims.quote: the stopped-clock illusion , where the second hand of an analog clock appears to stay still for longer than normal when first looked at

claims.claim: After a quick eye movement (saccade) the new target is overestimated in duration
claims.quote: This elicits an overestimation in the temporal duration for which that target stimulus (i.e., postsaccadic stimulus) was perceived.

claims.claim: Effect can extend apparent durations by up to half a second (probe 1 answer)
claims.quote: This effect can extend apparent durations by up to half a second

claims.claim: Visual information collected during a saccade is suppressed (probe 2 true)
claims.quote: visual information collected by the eyes during a saccade is suppressed through a process known as saccadic masking

claims.claim: The gap in perception is "filled in" with information gathered after the saccade
claims.quote: the gap in perception is "filled in" with information gathered after the saccade

claims.claim: Probe 1 distractors "Up to 5 seconds", "Up to a minute", "Up to two seconds" are all wrong
claims.quote: This effect can extend apparent durations by up to half a second
claims.note: Each distractor exceeds the stated maximum of half a second, so none can be true.
